preamble: Unrounding and lowering of the short close front rounded vowel [y] to the open-mid front unrounded [ɛ] is a regional development, known from the Kentish (south-eastern) dialect of English. Before the written records begin, Kentish had already unrounded short /y/ to /e/; most Modern English words go back to the Anglian outcome /ɪ/, but a handful kept the Kentish vowel, which surfaces in Modern English as /ɛ/: merry, knell, left, dent and the pronunciation of bury. This cell records those Modern English /ɛ/ reflexes; the Old English-stage merger itself, including the long vowel ȳ > ē, is filed under y_to_e.
